findings.evidence: Both statements have an `(... : ℂ)` LHS: line 134 `(‖qVector n φ‖ : ℂ) ^ 2 =` and line 189 `(twoParticleCorrelation n φ : ℂ) =`. No real-valued expansion exists in the file (grep for `norm_qVector_sq` finds only `integrable_norm_qVector_sq`, `integral_norm_qVector_sq` and `norm_qVector_sq_eq_card_add_mul_twoParticleCorrelation`, none of which expands the pair sum).
findings.fix: Add the real forms, e.g. `norm_qVector_sq : ‖qVector n φ‖ ^ 2 = Fintype.card ι + ∑ j, ∑ k ∈ univ.erase j, (fourier n (φ j - φ k)).re` and the matching `twoParticleCorrelation_eq_sum`, derived from the existing cast lemmas via `Complex.ofReal_injective`. Using `fourier n (φ j - φ k)` (the `fourier_eval_sub` this PR adds) also makes the statement match the module docstring's "average of `e^{i n (φⱼ - φₖ)}`" and the cosine average of Bilandzic et al. §II.
findings.issue: `twoParticleCorrelation` and `‖qVector n φ‖ ^ 2` are ℝ-valued, but their only pair-sum expansions are the ℂ-cast forms `ofReal_norm_qVector_sq` (line 133) and `ofReal_twoParticleCorrelation_eq_sum` (line 188). Every real-side consumer must redo the cast gymnastics the author performs at lines 389-391 (`apply Complex.ofReal_injective; rw [← integral_complex_ofReal]; push_cast`); the §5.1 variance bullet and §5.2 will hit the same wall.

findings.evidence: `qVector_zero` and `anisotropyCoeff_zero` exist at lines 98-100 and 244-247; grep for `twoParticleCorrelation_` yields `_def`, `_eq_zero_of_card_le_one`, `_neg`, `_add_const`, `_eq_sum` and the integral/integrability lemmas, with no `n = 0` value.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] theorem twoParticleCorrelation_zero (h : 1 < Fintype.card ι) (φ : ι → AddCircle T) : twoParticleCorrelation 0 φ = 1`; from `qVector_zero` one gets `‖Q₀‖ = M`, so `(M ^ 2 - M) / (M * (M - 1)) = 1`.
findings.issue: The `n = 0` value is part of the characteristic API the file develops — `qVector_zero` (line 99) and `anisotropyCoeff_zero` (line 245) are both there and both `@[simp]` — but `twoParticleCorrelation` has none, even though it is the definition the roadmap's §5.2 builds `vn{2}` on. This is also the sharp case of `abs_twoParticleCorrelation_le_one`.

summary: The surface is minimal, bodies are unexposed, and there is no compatibility layer, but the characteristic API of the ℝ-valued `twoParticleCorrelation` is incomplete: its only expansion lemmas are `Complex.ofReal` casts, and the `n = 0` value is given for `qVector` and `anisotropyCoeff` but not for the headline definition.
